2027-06-02.title: Third Wednesday of the Apostles
2027-06-02.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Shine like stars in the world
This is truly the Saviour of the world
2027-06-02.alt: Season of the Apostles (Šleehe), from Pentecost to the beginning of the Season of Summer (Kaitha): the Church remembers the apostles who, filled with the Holy Spirit, preached Christ and founded the Churches, among them the Church of India founded by Mar Thoma. The Holy Qurbana is celebrated with the Anaphora of Addai and Mari, and the Angel of the Lord (Angelus) is prayed at the three hours of the day. In the Latin calendar today is the optional memorial of Sts Marcellinus and Peter, martyrs.
2027-06-02.verse: They said to the woman, “It is no longer because of what you said that we believe, for we have heard for ourselves, and we know that this is truly the Savior of the world.”
theo: The Gospel today is the last scene of one of the great encounters of John's Gospel. At Jacob's well, at noon, Jesus has asked a Samaritan woman for a drink, and he has given her living water instead. She has left her water jar and run back to her town with a strange message: come and see a man who told me everything I have ever done. Now we hear what happened next: “Many Samaritans from that city believed in him because of the woman’s testimony.” This is remarkable on every side. Jews and Samaritans did not share vessels or prayers; the woman herself, it seems, was not well regarded in her own town; and yet her word is enough to bring a whole crowd out to the well. She did not preach a sermon. She told what had happened to her. That is the first form of witness that the Season of the Apostles asks of each of us: not a lecture about religion, but the honest story of what the Lord has done in my life. Only a few years later the deacon Philip would go down to a city of Samaria and proclaim the Messiah there, “so there was great joy in that city” (Acts 8:8); in a sense the woman at the well had already prepared the ground.

Then the Samaritans do something beautiful: “So when the Samaritans came to him, they asked him to stay with them; and he stayed there two days. And many more believed because of his word.” They do not only want to see the wonder-worker; they want him as a guest. And Jesus, who was on a journey to Galilee, stays. Faith grows in the time spent with him. Finally they say to the woman: “It is no longer because of what you said that we believe, for we have heard for ourselves, and we know that this is truly the Savior of the world.” This is the goal of all witness. The witness brings people to Jesus and then steps back, so that they may meet him themselves. A mother's prayers, a catechism teacher's patience, a friend's invitation to a retreat are all the woman's word; but sooner or later each person must hear him for themselves, in the Scriptures, in the Holy Qurbana, in silent prayer. And notice who first gives Jesus this great title: not the disciples, not the leaders in Jerusalem, but Samaritans, outsiders. The Saviour of the world is recognised first by those whom the world kept at a distance.

Paul's letter to the Philippians speaks to a community that already believes and must now grow. “Therefore, my beloved, just as you have always obeyed me, not only in my presence, but much more now in my absence, work out your own salvation with fear and trembling; for it is God who is at work in you, enabling you both to will and to work for his good pleasure.” Two truths are held together here. We must work; salvation is not something that happens to us while we sleep. Yet the very wanting and the very working are God's gift in us. The Catholic faith has always kept this balance: grace comes first and carries us, and grace calls for our answer. Then Paul gives a practical rule: “Do all things without murmuring and arguing, so that you may be blameless and innocent, children of God without blemish in the midst of a crooked and perverse generation, in which you shine like stars in the world.” The murmuring of Israel in the wilderness is in the background. A grumbling Christian is a dim star. A family that does not complain at every inconvenience, an office worker who does not join the gossip, a young person who refuses the cynical joke, shine in a dark sky. The secret, Paul says, is “holding fast to the word of life”: the same word of Jesus that the Samaritans heard for themselves.
outline: A woman runs to her town; a whole people comes to the well.
Point 1 · The witness of one woman
Not a sermon but a story: what the Lord has done for me.
Point 2 · We have heard for ourselves
They ask him to stay; faith grows in time spent with Jesus.
Point 3 · God at work in you
Work out your salvation; grace comes first and calls for our answer.
Without murmuring, holding fast to the word of life.
“This is truly the Savior of the world.”
live: Share with one person this week, simply, one thing the Lord has done in your life.
Spend an extra ten minutes with the Gospel or before the Blessed Sacrament on two days this week.
Go one whole day without complaining, and notice how often you are tempted.
fathers: First they believed because of the woman's report; then, when he stayed with them, they believed because of his presence. So it happens now with those outside the Church: Christ is announced to them by friends, they come, and he remains with them; and he stays two days, that is, he gives them the two commandments of love.

The woman did what the apostles were later sent to do. She did not hide what had been said about her life, but went running into the city and called everyone. Her shame became her preaching, and from her word a whole city came to the Lord.
magis: The transmission of the Christian faith consists primarily in proclaiming Jesus Christ in order to lead others to faith in him.
The preparation of man for the reception of grace is already a work of grace; God completes in us what he has begun.
Lay people fulfil their prophetic mission by evangelization, that is, the proclamation of Christ by word and the testimony of life.
saints: Latin calendar: Sts Marcellinus, priest, and Peter, exorcist, martyrs at Rome in the persecution of Diocletian (about 304); their names are among the martyrs remembered in the Roman Canon.

1–6 June: the third and fourth weeks of the Season of the Apostles. Tue 1: St Justin, martyr. Thu 3: in the Latin calendar, St Charles Lwanga and his companions, the Martyrs of Uganda. Fri 4: the Feast of the Sacred Heart of Jesus (Third Friday of the Apostles), and First Friday. Sat 5: the Feast of the Immaculate Heart of Mary (Third Saturday of the Apostles); in the Latin calendar also St Boniface. Sun 6: Fourth Sunday of the Apostles. June is the month of the Sacred Heart in popular devotion; in Kerala it is also the month the schools reopen and the monsoon rains arrive.
2027-06-02.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, Saviour of the world, you sat by the well and gave living water to a Samaritan woman, and through her word you drew a whole town to yourself. Make us witnesses who tell simply what you have done for us. Stay with us, Lord, so that we may hear you for ourselves. Father, you are at work in us, giving us both the will and the strength to do your pleasure: keep us from murmuring, and let us shine like stars, holding fast to the word of life. Glory to the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, now and for ever. Amen.
altar: The Samaritans asked Jesus to stay with them, and he stayed. In every Holy Qurbana he comes to stay with us, not two days but in our very bodies; let us receive him as our guest and go out to tell others, as the woman did, what he has done for us.

2027-06-02.action: Tell one person, simply, what the Lord has done for you, and spend one whole day without complaining.
2027-06-02.question: Do I believe only because of what others told me, or have I heard Jesus for myself?

family.explain: A woman met Jesus at a well. She was so happy that she ran to her town and told everyone, “Come and see!” The people came, and they asked Jesus to stay. After two days they said, “Now we believe, not only because you told us, but because we have heard him ourselves.” Our parents and teachers tell us about Jesus, but Jesus wants to be our own friend too. We meet him when we pray, when we read the Bible and when we go to the Holy Qurbana.
family.intention: We pray for people who have never heard of Jesus, and for missionaries who bring him to them.
family.ask: Ask: “How can each of us spend a little time alone with Jesus this week?”

illus: A young engineer from Pala, studying for a master's degree in Germany, was asked by a classmate why he still went to Mass when so few of his friends did. He thought for a moment and said: ‘When I was small, I went because my grandmother took me. She used to pray the rosary in a loud voice on the verandah every evening, and I prayed because she did. When I came here, I stopped for almost a year. Then one night, alone and anxious before an exam, I went into an empty church and sat there for an hour. I cannot explain it, but I knew he was there. Now I do not go because my grandmother told me. I go because I have met him myself.’ On his next visit home he told his grandmother the story. She only laughed and said, ‘That is all I was praying for.’

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Saviour of the world, we gather around you as the Samaritans gathered at the well. Stay with us, speak to us, and let us hear you for ourselves. Amen.
share: Many Samaritans believed because of the woman’s testimony (John 4:39). Whose witness first brought me to Jesus?
They asked him to stay with them (John 4:40). Do I give Jesus time to stay with me?
It is God who is at work in you (Philippians 2:13). Where do I see God at work in me now?
Do all things without murmuring (Philippians 2:14). What do I grumble about most?
interc: For the Church in this Season of the Apostles, that every believer may become a witness like the woman at the well.
For people who live far from the Church, that they may hear Christ for themselves.
For catechism teachers and parents who hand on the faith, that their words may lead children to a personal meeting with Jesus.
For families and communities torn by complaining and quarrels, that they may learn gratitude.
For missionaries, that the Saviour of the world may be known through them.
pm.close: Father, you sent your Son as the Saviour of the world and you are at work in us by your Spirit. Make us witnesses of what we have seen and heard, keep us from murmuring, and let us shine like stars in this generation. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today a whole town comes to Jesus because of one woman. She was not a priest or a scholar. She simply ran home and said: come and see a man who told me everything I have ever done. Many believed because of her word (John 4:39).
That is how faith spreads, in the time of the apostles and today: through ordinary people who tell what the Lord has done for them. Each of us has such a story. Let us not keep it hidden.

But the Samaritans went further. They asked Jesus to stay, and he stayed two days. Then they said to the woman: now we believe not because of what you said, but because we have heard for ourselves; this is truly the Saviour of the world (John 4:42). Our parents gave us the faith; but each of us must also meet Jesus personally, in prayer, in the Word and in the Holy Qurbana.

Saint Paul tells the Philippians: work out your salvation with fear and trembling, for it is God who is at work in you (Philippians 2:12–13). God gives the will and the strength; we must give our answer. Let us not be lazy with grace.

And he adds: do all things without murmuring, and you will shine like stars in the world. A Christian who complains about everything gives little light. Let us thank God instead, hold fast to his word, and shine where we live and work. Amen.
kids: Children, a woman met Jesus and ran to tell everyone in her town. Then the people met Jesus themselves and loved him too!
Your parents and teachers tell you about Jesus. Now talk to Jesus yourself every day, like a friend. And try not to grumble today: be a little star!

God at work in us makes us lights in the world when we hold fast to the word of life.
2027-06-02.resolve: This week, tell your story of faith, give Jesus time to stay with you, and shine without murmuring.
